analysis.title: Nuscale Power Corp. (SMR): Manufacturing progress advances, while commercialization timing remains the key debate; Neutral
key_insights: GS stays Neutral on SMR with a 12-month price target of $4, cut from $6. Price was $4.37 at the 5 Nov 2026 close, implying 8.5% downside.

3Q26 revenue was $0.3mn against a GS estimate of $9.0mn. Management pointed to the Doosan agreement for First Article production of the NPM upper reactor coolant system as tangible progress toward commercialization.

Management said ENTRA1 continues to work toward a definitive PPA with TVA but gave no timeline, despite acknowledging the process has been lengthy. GS calls limited visibility into definitive customer agreements the key catalyst for SMR.

A PPA between ENTRA1 and TVA would not itself be a module order. It would trigger pre-delivery work (COLA and engineering), followed by an OEM agreement between SMR and ENTRA1 for the eventual sale of modules.
Management said about 50%-60% of the COLA work completed for the Carbon Free Power Project should be transferable to another customer.

SMR is investing in long-lead materials that will sit as inventory/WIP on the balance sheet and be recovered through module sales under future OEM agreements. It also continues fuel design work with Framatome and safety instrumentation and controls work with Paragon, and is pursuing dual or tertiary sourcing across most supply packages.
SMR ended 3Q26 with about $1.9bn of liquidity. Management believes this funds first article fabrication, engineering and licensing readiness ahead of an ENTRA1 OEM agreement.
Quarterly opex was about $65mn and management expects it to stay fairly constant near term. Spending is expected to rise as commercial projects begin and flow through opex and COGS.
RoPower visibility is limited. Management is in dialogue with RoPower and Nuclearelectrica after Romania's new government formed, and has requested a meeting with the new administration.
GS cut 2026 sales to $20mn (-30%) and left 2027 and 2028 unchanged at $118mn and $206mn. EPS estimates for 2026-2028 moved to -$0.52, -$0.38 and -$0.43, from -$0.50, -$0.34 and -$0.37.

The price target rests on a 50/50 weighting of DCF and EV/Sales. GS raised WACC to about 22.5% from 20% and cut the terminal multiple to 5X from 8X, citing greater commercialization timing uncertainty and lower comps. The EV/Sales leg keeps a 1X multiple on 2030E revenue.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $4 from $6 on a higher WACC and lower terminal multiple, reflecting commercialization timing uncertainty. Manufacturing progress is an incremental positive but customer agreement visibility is limited.

earnings_insights: SMR 3Q26 (quarter ended Sep-26) reported revenue $0.3mn vs GS estimate $9.0mn and $8.2mn in Sep-25.
SMR 3Q26 reported EPS (basic and diluted) -$0.11 vs GS estimate -$0.13. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was -$0.11 vs GS estimate -$0.13.
SMR 3Q26 reported total operating expenses $65.0mn vs GS estimate $67.0mn. SG&A was $18.0mn vs $30.0mn estimated and R&D was $19.0mn vs $18.4mn estimated.
SMR 3Q26 reported adj. EBITDA -$64.5mn vs GS estimate -$62.1mn. Net interest expense was $19.1mn vs $6.7mn estimated.
SMR 3Q26 reported operating cash flow -$28.6mn vs GS estimate +$808.5mn. Reported free cash flow to equity was -$28.7mn.
GS 2026E revenue estimate is $20.0mn (prior $28.8mn), with 2027E $118.1mn and 2028E $206.0mn unchanged. 2026E-2028E adj. EBITDA estimates are -$253.9mn, -$243.8mn and -$236.6mn.
GS 4Q26E EPS estimate is -$0.15, with 1Q27E at -$0.08 and 2Q27E at -$0.09.
risk_factors: Execution risk and customer concentration or dependence
End cost for modules upon delivery
Uncertain timing of the TVA PPA and the follow-on OEM agreement
geopolitical: Romania's new government has formed and SMR has requested a meeting to understand its direction on the RoPower project with Nuclearelectrica.
